implemented: Explicit boolean enabled=true required; default false does not invoke register/enqueue/send adapters
No startup import, scheduler, route, credentials, environment variables, migration or provider SDK
One-job worker policy with 30-second leased claim, max 3 attempts, 5-second send timeout, 24-hour TTL, Retry-After and exponential jitter
Current session/conversation authorization plus binding revision/consent check before send; atomic final repository check
Minimal generic envelope with opaque binding/event tags; no account/email/chat body/roster/health/finance fields
Revoke remains available when sender disabled; repository must match authenticated principal/session and optional installation

coreAPI.trustedIdentity: principalId + sessionId are opaque server-resolved IDs, not email, raw JWT, request-body ownership claims or push endpoints. HTTP adapters MUST authenticate and construct this object. Core has no HTTP endpoint.
coreAPI.subscribe: Validate explicit consent, server-issued/proven installationId, opaque targetRef and transport webpush|fcm. Authorize current authenticated session, then atomic repository.bind. Ownership of installation and provider target must be proven by future adapter; arbitrary client-chosen refs are not authority.
coreAPI.revoke: Trusted server logout/consent/revocation integration calls revoke(actor, optional installationId); actor is constructed from verified session or trusted server revocation event, never raw body. No new permission request.
coreAPI.enqueueInTransaction: After authorized chat write, pass SAME database transaction; event={messageId,threadId,recipientIds,occurredAt}. Use stable persisted message ID from PR894 and original persisted occurrence time. Derive recipients from server relationships, not request body. No earlier message backfill after new consent.
coreAPI.runOne: Caller provides bounded scheduling/concurrency only after separate activation review. No timers or background scheduler start at import/factory.

repositoryContract.durability: Future durable transactional adapter is required. Test fixture in scripts/tests/fixtures is memory-only and must never be used in production. Its passing tests are not evidence of real SQL isolation, crash persistence, provider behavior or physical delivery.
repositoryContract.bind: Atomically maintain one active owner+session per installation and uniqueness of active transport target. Reject takeover of any active installation/target. Duplicate identical registration preserves revision/bindingTag/consentAt. Rotation/re-consent increments revision, creates new opaque bindingTag and invalidates old queued deliveries. Account switch must revoke old binding before new registration.
repositoryContract.revoke: Atomically match principal+session; optionally installation. Disable consent, increment revision and cancel pending deliveries or make claim/check reject them. Trusted account deletion/visitor revocation must cover all relevant sessions, not just the browser currently open.
repositoryContract.enqueue: In the SAME message transaction insert only currently active, consenting authorized-recipient bindings at event occurrence time; unique (messageId,principalId,installationId,revision). Stable opaque eventId stored with winner, not regenerated per retry. Store metadata only; raw target credentials live in a separate protected registry referenced by targetRef. Rollback of message write must roll back delivery insertion.
repositoryContract.claim: Atomically select due nonterminal row; expired leases recover after restart. Increment attempts when claiming; refuse >=3 attempts and expired TTL even after crash. Set unique token+leaseUntil and return immutable snapshot. Bound query/batch sizes and retention; no infinite retry.
repositoryContract.loadBinding: Read current trusted installation binding, revision, session, consent and targetRef.
repositoryContract.canDispatch: Atomic final recheck of exact lease token, live lease, expiry, active binding, same principal/session/revision/tag and consent. Return false on lost lease/revocation. Provider submission after this check can still race revocation; already submitted notifications cannot be reliably recalled.
repositoryContract.settle: Compare-and-set by deliveryId+current unexpired lease token. Stale worker must not overwrite another attempt. Terminal state sent/failed/expired/cancelled/exhausted; retry stores nextAt and clears lease. Recover errors without logging secrets.
repositoryContract.disableBinding: Compare installationId+revision before disabling expired provider target; late failure from an old revision must not disable a new registration.

authorizationContract.subscribe: Return literal true only for current authorized session and device registration consent.
authorizationContract.deliver: Immediately before dispatch validate current session, recipient account, current colleague/visitor relation, visitor status, chat permission and message/thread access. Deleted/revoked account, expired JWT/session, revoked invitation, opt-out or denied relationship returns false. Outage throws -> bounded retry with no send.

providerContract.send: Injected only after review. Receives {transport,targetRef,payload,ttlSeconds,signal}. Resolve targetRef via trusted registry; implement real Web Push encryption/VAPID or FCM OAuth outside this patch. Never fetch arbitrary user URL. Validate provider endpoints, DNS/IP destinations and redirect policy before permitting outbound requests.
providerContract.result: Normalized {status: integer, retryAfter?: HTTP Retry-After string, expired?: boolean}. Only map known provider expired subscription errors to expired=true with 404/410. Provider auth/config failure is terminal for this attempt, not an unlimited retry loop.
providerContract.abort: Adapter must honor AbortSignal and transport-level timeout. A timeout after provider acceptance is ambiguous; retry reuses same eventId. No exactly-once delivery guarantee.
providerContract.secrets: No values inspected or generated. VAPID pair/contact and approved FCM project/app+delivery identity remain unverified and require separate approval if missing. No new grants/service account/signing key.

clientHandoff.receiver: Mobile Core validates version/type/size and exact current bindingTag from origin-private/native private state before showing generic notification. Unknown/stale binding or no active session must be discarded; never broadcast account data. Durable bounded dedup keyed by bindingTag+eventId with TTL; stable OS tag is supplementary, not exactly-once proof.
clientHandoff.logout: Clear/invalidate local bindingTag first, revoke registration on server, cancel local matching notifications where supported and stop old-token routing. Offline logout must immediately prevent local display and queue server revocation for next authenticated opportunity; process death/race limitations need explicit physical tests.
clientHandoff.click: Fixed origin-relative app entry only. Reauthenticate and fetch authorized inbox after opening; no payload-provided URL/thread/account authority and no implicit read acknowledgement. If login changed, drop old binding intent.
clientHandoff.PWA: Preserve #825 PDF cache/share handling; add push/notificationclick only through owner-reviewed composition. Browser permission/subscription requires explicit user action/consent. This core does not subscribe devices.
clientHandoff.Android: Owner implements token rotation, registration and receiver lifecycle with existing notification consent/channel policy. No additional OS permission proposed. Compatible approved signing/version and physical tests required; do not use incompatible old AAB.
clientHandoff.Wake: Chat update transport is best effort and never substitutes local exact alarms or promises force-stop/reboot alarm delivery.
